walkthrough:
**What does volatility really mean?**

Volatility tells us how easily a liquid turns to vapour. A more volatile substance has weaker forces between its molecules, so molecules escape easily.

Think: separating molecules, not breaking molecules apart.

**Identify the forces between halogen molecules**

Chlorine, bromine and iodine exist as diatomic molecules: $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$, $\text{I}_2$. They are non-polar, so the only forces between molecules are London dispersion forces.

$$\text{intermolecular force} = \text{London dispersion forces only}$$

**Link electrons to strength of dispersion forces**

Down the group, each molecule has more electrons: $\text{Cl}_2$ has 34, $\text{Br}_2$ has 70, $\text{I}_2$ has 106. More electrons means a larger, more polarisable electron cloud, so stronger temporary dipoles form.

$$\text{more electrons} \rightarrow \text{stronger London forces} \rightarrow \text{higher boiling point} \rightarrow \text{lower volatility}$$

**Conclude the trend**

That is why chlorine is a gas, bromine is a volatile liquid and iodine is a solid at room temperature. The decrease in volatility is caused by the increasing number of electrons strengthening the intermolecular forces.

options.A: Bond length does increase down the group, but it describes the covalent bond inside the $\text{X}_2$ molecule. Volatility depends on breaking forces between molecules, not on the distance within one molecule.
options.B: Bond strength describes how hard it is to break the covalent X-X bond to form atoms. Vaporisation does not break covalent bonds, it only overcomes weak London forces between intact molecules.
options.C: Electronegativity does decrease down Group 17, but all the halogen molecules are non-polar. Polarity is not the controlling factor here, the strength of London dispersion forces is.
options.D: Correct. The number of electrons increases from $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{I}_2$. This gives stronger London dispersion forces between molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them and volatility decreases down the group.
